title: Unit – 4 : Session – 4/5 : SLO – 2  |  Structures, Control and Backtracking in Prolog
sections: 1. b) Backtracking — Prolog systematically returns to earlier choice points to explore alternative solutions.
1. In logic programming, control flow is governed by unification and resolution (goal satisfaction).
2. Backtracking is used to try alternative solutions when the current one fails.
Prolog executes goals depth-first, left-to-right, matching clause heads by unification.
On failure, the engine backtracks to the most recent choice point and tries the next matching clause.
